item.title: Singapore tops religious diversity; global trends show Christians largest, Muslims fastest-growing, Hindus near 15%
item.description: Singapore ranks as the world’s most religiously diverse nation in a 2026 study by Pew Research Center, scoring 9.3 on its Religious Diversity Index. Covering 201 countries and drawing on 2,700 censuses, the report tracks global shifts: Christians remain largest, Muslims grow fastest, the unaffiliated reach 24.2%, and Asia-Pacific emerges most diverse regionally.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: 'My insufficient command of English': Mark Rutte explains why he called Trump ‘daddy,' says 'I am living with it'
item.description: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte clarified his use of the term "Daddy" for Donald Trump, attributing it to a language slip-up during a discussion about Iran's nuclear facilities. Rutte described the remark as unintentional, stemming from his "insufficient command of the English language." He acknowledged Trump's good-natured reaction, noting the nickname's subsequent viral spread.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ohio Senator Jon Husted voted to block Epstein files after donation from Leslie Wexner: Report
item.description: Ohio Republican Senator Jon Husted is under scrutiny for voting to block the release of Jeffrey Epstein files shortly after receiving a $3,500 campaign donation from Leslie Wexner, a former associate of the convicted sex offender. This donation is part of over $116,000 Husted has received from Wexner throughout his career.

item.title: What happened to influencer Clavicular at Arizona State University fashion show that led to framemogging trend
item.description: “Clavicular Framemogging” is a viral internet slang phrase that began after influencer Clavicular appeared at an Arizona State University fashion show. A video showing him beside a larger fraternity member led users to joke that he was “framemogged.” The strange sounding phrase quickly turned into memes, proving how fast online culture creates and spreads new slang.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: Jonathan Horst returns to YouTube with Thinking Different after Mac Address hiatus and Linus Media Group exit
item.description: Jonathan Horst, former Mac Address host under Linus Media Group, has returned to YouTube with a new independent channel called “Thinking Different.” He announced the comeback on X on February 12, 2026. After leaving during 2024 layoffs, Horst shared gratitude for his time at Mac Address and now plans broader tech content beyond Apple.

item.title: ‘I know this disease will kill me’: RFK Jr admits snorting cocaine off toilet seats, non-profit org calls on him to 'resign'
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. stated he isn't afraid of germs due to past cocaine use, reflecting on his addiction battle. Critics, including Protect Our Care, are calling for his resignation, citing his unsuitability for the role. Kennedy's past drug offenses and vaccine skepticism have also drawn scrutiny.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'Deception and farce': Sheikh Hasina rejects Bangladesh poll results, calls it 'disgraceful chapter'
item.description: Former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina, living in exile, has branded the recent February 12 polls a 'pre-planned election of deception and farce.' She alleges widespread manipulation and unrealistic turnout figures. Meanwhile, her rival Khaleda Zia's party, the BNP, secured a significant victory, prompting calls for Hasina's extradition from India to face trial.

item.title: Bombshell report claims Trump ‘uncomfortable’ with Noem and Lewandowski’s relationship; DHS chief fired Coast Guard pilot over her missing blanket
item.description: A bombshell report alleges Secretary Kristi Noem's Department of Homeland Security is in "constant chaos," driven by headline-grabbing crackdowns and internal power struggles. Sources claim Noem prioritized personal image with staged photo-ops and sidelined critics, while her adviser Lewandowski allegedly sought a badge and gun without proper training.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 'She’s never been in jail': Marine war veteran pleads for assistance after ICE arrested his wife during interview for permanent resident card
item.description: A U.S. Marine veteran is seeking help after his wife, Diana Butnarciuc, was arrested by ICE during an interview for a permanent resident card. Butnarciuc, who arrived in 2008 and has no criminal record, faces a 2018 deportation order. Her husband filed an I-130 petition, and they await a resolution to her immigration status.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Unborn babies are now treated as human beings’: Puerto Rico signs historic law recognising the fetus
item.description: Puerto Rico's governor signed a law recognizing unborn children as human beings in criminal cases, aiming to punish violence against pregnant women. While officials insist it doesn't ban abortion, critics fear this legal shift could undermine reproductive rights and medical autonomy, sparking widespread debate and unease among medical professionals.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: India's Sheikh Hasina dilemma: Resurgent BNP seems set to press extradition demand - what are New Delhi's options?
item.description: As Bangladesh's new government, led by the BNP, takes charge of country's affair, it has called on India for the extradition of ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who is in New Delhi. This demand presents a significant diplomatic challenge for India. Dhaka says, it seeks a relationship based on equality and mutual respect, with border security and water sharing also key issues.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Even US won't be powerful to go alone’: German chancellor calls for revival of trans-Atlantic ties
item.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz urged the US and Europe to jointly rebuild trans-Atlantic trust amidst rising global rivalries, warning against isolationism. He emphasized a "new trans-Atlantic partnership," distancing Europe from US "culture wars" and advocating for free trade. Merz highlighted Europe's increased defense spending and commitment to a stronger European pillar within NATO, signaling a shift towards greater shared responsibility.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk
